What a /29 means

A /29 is a very small subnet (6 usable hosts), suited to management segments, DMZ hand-offs or links with a handful of devices.

The prefix length is the number of leading bits that identify the network. A /29 uses 29 network bits and leaves 3 host bits, so the block contains 8 addresses. Usable hosts: 2(32−29) − 2 = 8 − 2 = 6.

Configuration examples

Cisco IOS

interface Vlan10
 ip address 192.168.1.1 255.255.255.248
!
access-list 10 permit 192.168.1.0 0.0.0.7

Juniper Junos

set interfaces ge-0/0/0 unit 0 family inet address 192.168.1.1/29

Linux

ip addr add 192.168.1.1/29 dev eth0

Addresses shown are examples from private or documentation space. Replace them with your own plan.

FAQ

How many usable hosts are in a /29?

6. A /29 has 8 addresses; the first is the network address and the last is the broadcast address, so 6 are usable.

What is the subnet mask for /29?

255.255.255.248. The wildcard mask, used in ACLs and OSPF network statements, is 0.0.0.7.
